shortDescription: The German spot energy prices rose on Tuesday as solar power production was set to fall.($1 = 0.8675 euros)

children: The German spot energy prices rose on Tuesday as solar power production was set to fall.
The German day-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBD1) was up by 6.7% to €186 ($214) per megawatt-hour at 0648 GMT, according to LSEG data.
Solar power was expected to fall by 2.5 gigawatts to 12.7 GW and wind power to rise by 2.2 GW to 13.4 GW, with consumption expected to edge up by 0.7 GW to 54.7 GW.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was up 2.4% to €185/MWh, according to LSEG data.
Wind power was expected to rise by 1.6 GW in France, while solar power generation was set to fall by nearly 1 GW. Consumption, on the other hand, was seen edging 0.4 GW lower.

"Strong wind should weigh on spot prices into the weekend, but the subsequent wind drop and persistently low hydro create upward pressure from Monday September 21st," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan wrote.
French nuclear availability rose by 7 percentage points to 80% of total capacity.
EDF's St. Alban plant will reduce power output at its two reactors by 2.2 GW on Wednesday due to environmental constraints, the French utility said.

Tuesday's strike has cut French electricity supply by 6.7 GW, data from EDF showed. That equals about 15% of total power demand in the early hours, but does not affect the country's status as a net exporter, data from grid operator RTE showed.
On a year-ahead basis, neither the French (TRFRBYc1) nor the German (TRDEBYc1) contracts were trading, according to LSEG data.
